So we may use integration by parts to estimate $Z_2$; letting \[ v_\ell(\xi) := \sum_{\substack{(r, a_ik_i) = 1 \\ \ell \mid r \le \xi}} \frac{r}{\varphi(r)}\ \textnormal{e} \left(- \frac{a_1 h\overline{r}}{a_2k_2} \right), \] which can be bounded via \cref{lem:incomplete-weil} (with $n = a_1 h$, $c = a_2k_2$, $d = r$ and $k = a_1k_1$), we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} Z_2(\ell) = \int u(\xi) dv_\ell(\xi) = - \int v_\ell(\xi) du(\xi) &\ll \frac{x^{2\varepsilon}}{R^2} \sup_{\xi \in [R/2, 3R]} |v_\ell(\xi)| \\ &\ll_\varepsilon \frac{x^{3\varepsilon}}{R^2} \left((a_1 h, a_2 k_2)^{1/2}K^{1/2} + (a_1 h, a_2 k_2) \frac{R}{K} \right), \end{aligned} \] uniformly in $\ell \ge 1$. Returning to \cref{eq:Y2} and summing over $h$ and $k_2$, the GCD-terms contribute at most $O_\varepsilon(x^{\varepsilon})$ on average (since $(a_1, a_2) = 1$). Thus \[ \begin{aligned} Y_2 \ll_\varepsilon x^{4\varepsilon} |\mathscr{E}| |\chi_D| K^2 H \frac{1}{E} \frac{1}{R^2} \left(\sqrt{K} + \frac{R}{K} \right) &\le x^{7\varepsilon} \frac{K^2}{MR} \left(\sqrt{K} + \frac{R}{K} \right) \\ &\ll x^{7\varepsilon - 1} \left(\frac{K^{7/2}}{R} + K^2\right). \end{aligned} \] By \cref{eq:conditions}, we have $K^{3/2} \ll x^{1-9\varepsilon}$ and $R \ll x^{1-11\varepsilon}$, so we get a final bound of $Y_2 \ll_\varepsilon x^{-\varepsilon} K^2 / R$. This completes our proof of \cref{prop:dispersion-sums}.$(ii)$.
nodes.section: 7 The second and third dispersion sums
nodes.statement_short: Poisson expansion and Bézout reciprocity turn the $r$-sum into an incomplete Kloosterman-type sum, bounded by partial summation and the incomplete Weil bound.

nodes.name: Eliminating bad index pairs
nodes.statement: For $\varepsilon \ge \eta > 0$, under the parameter conditions in \cref{eq:conditions,eq:E-conditions}, one has \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0) X_1 = \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} \mathcal{E}_r(c) \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re} \\ k_i \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2 c} \pmod{r}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \qquad + O_\eta\left(x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R} \right), \end{aligned} \] where \begin{equation} \mathcal{K}(\eta) := \left\{ (k_1, k_2) \in \mathbf{N}^2\ \Big\vert\ \twolinemath{(k_1, (a_2k_2)^\infty) \le x^\eta,\ (k_2, (a_2k_1)^\infty) \le x^\eta,} { (k_1 - k_2, (a_2k_1k_2)^\infty) \le x^\eta,\ |k_1 - k_2| > K/x^\eta } \right\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Restricting $\mathcal S_1-\hat\Phi(0)X_1$ to pairs $(k_1,k_2)\in\mathcal K(\eta)$ costs only $O(x^{-\eta/4}K^2/R)$.
conclusions: \mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0) X_1 = \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} \mathcal{E}_r(c) \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re} \\ k_i \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2 c} \pmod{r}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \qquad + O_\eta\left(x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R} \right),
nodes.label: prop:bad-pairs

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.1
nodes.statement: We eliminate the contribution of several sets of pairs $(k_1, k_2)$, putting absolute values on all the coefficients involved; thus it does not matter if some of these eliminated sets have nonempty intersections. First, we consider the almost-diagonal pairs with $|k_1 - k_2| \le K/x^\eta$, which contribute to $\mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0)X_1$ at most \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{E}_r(c)| \sum_{\substack{k_1 \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2c} \pmod{r} \\ (k_1, e) = 1}} |u_{k_1}| \sum_{\substack{k_2 \equiv k_1 \pmod{re} \\ |k_1 - k_2| \le K/x^\eta}} |u_{k_2}| \\ &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/2} E R \left(\frac{K}{R} + 1\right) \left(\frac{K}{x^\eta RE} + 1\right) \\ &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/2}ER \frac{K}{R} \frac{K}{x^\eta RE} \\ &\asymp x^{-\eta/2} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] where we used that $\sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{E}_r(c)| \le \frac{1}{M} \sum_m \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) + \widehat{\Phi}(0) \ll 1$, and that $x^{\eta} RE \ll K$ (which follows from \cref{eq:E-conditions} and $\eta \le \varepsilon$). Then, we consider those pairs with $v := (k_1, k_2) > x^{\eta/2}$. Their contribution to $\mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0)X_1$ is at most \[ \ll \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{E}_r(c)| \sum_{\substack{b \in (\mathbf{Z}/re\mathbf{Z})^\times \\ b \equiv a_1\overline{a_2c} \pmod{r}}} \sum_{\substack{v > x^{\eta/2} \\ (v,re)=1}} \left(\sum_{\substack{k \equiv b \pmod{re} \\ v \mid k}} |u_k| \right)^2. \] Using that $(v, re) = 1$, we can bound one inner sum over $k$ by $\ll_\eta x^{\eta/8}(K(vRE)^{-1} + 1) \ll x^{-3\eta/8}K(RE)^{-1}$ (recall that $x^{\eta} RE \ll K$ by \cref{eq:E-conditions}). This yields a total contribution of \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll_\eta \frac{K}{REx^{3\eta/8}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{E}_r(c)| \sum_{\substack{v > x^\eta \\ (v,re)=1}} \sum_{\substack{k \equiv a_1\overline{a_2c} \pmod{r} \\ v \mid k}} |u_k| \\ &\le \frac{K}{Rx^{3\eta/8}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{c \in (\mathbf{Z}/r\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{E}_r(c)| \sum_{\substack{k \equiv a_1\overline{a_2c} \pmod{r}}} \tau(k) |u_k| \\ &\ll_\eta \frac{K}{Rx^{2\eta/8}} R \left(\frac{K}{R} + 1\right) \\ &\ll x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] which is also acceptable. Keeping the notation $v = (k_1, k_2)$, which we may now assume is at most $x^{\eta/2}$, note that \[ d_1 := (k_1, (a_2k_2)^\infty) = (k_1, (a_2 v)^\infty), \] and let us consider those pairs $(k_1, k_2)$ with $d_1 > x^\eta$. These contribute to $\mathcal{S}_1$ at most \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{(m, r) = 1} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{k_1 \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2m} \pmod{r} \\ (k_1, re) = 1,\ d_1 \mid k_1}} |u_{k_1}| \sum_{\substack{k_2 \equiv k_1 \pmod{re} \\ (k_1, k_2) = v}} |u_{k_2}| \\ &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/8} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{(m, r) = 1} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, re) = 1,\ d_1 \mid k_1 \\ r \mid a_2 m k_1 - a_1}} \left(\frac{K}{REv} + 1\right) \\ &\ll x^{\eta/8} \frac{K}{RE} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \frac{1}{v} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{m} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{d_1 \mid k_1}} \sum_{\substack{(r,m a_1a_2)=1 \\ r \mid a_2 m k_1 - a_1}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right), \end{aligned} \] where we used that $x^{\eta/2} RE \ll K$ and swapped sums. Considering the cases $a_2 m k_1 = a_1$ and $a_2 m k_1 - a_1 \neq 0$ separately, this is further bounded by \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll x^{\eta/8} \frac{K}{RE} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \frac{1}{v} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \left(\tau(|a_1|)^2 R + \sum_{m} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \mid (a_2v)^\infty \\ d_1 \le 4K}} \sum_{\substack{d_1 \mid k_1 \\ a_2 m k_1 \neq a_1}} \tau(|a_2 m k_1 - a_1|) \right) \\ &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/4}K + x^{\eta/4} \frac{K}{RE} \max_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{m} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \mid (a_2v)^\infty \\ d_1 \le 4K}} \left(\frac{K}{d_1} + 1\right) \\ &\ll x^{\eta/4}K + x^{1 + \eta/4} \frac{K}{R} \max_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_1 \le 4K \\ d_1 \mid (a_2 v)^\infty }} \frac{K}{d_1} \\ &\ll_\eta x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] where we used that $K \gg x^{\varepsilon} \gg x^\eta$, $R \ll x^{1-\eta/2}$ (by \cref{eq:conditions}), and the majorization \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d \le 4K \\ d \mid b^\infty }} d^{-1} \le x^{-2\eta/3} \sum_{\substack{d \le 4K \\ d \mid b^\infty }} d^{-1/3} = x^{-2\eta/3} O(1)^{O(\log b / \log \log b)} \ll_\eta x^{-\eta/2}, \end{equation} which holds uniformly for $b \ll x$. The contribution of the pairs with $d_1 > x^\eta$ to $\widehat{\Phi}(0)X_1$ is simpler and similarly bounded, and the contribution of the pairs with $d_2 := (k_2, (a_2k_1)^\infty) = (k_2, (a_2v)^\infty)$ is bounded symmetrically. All that is left is to eliminate the contribution of the pairs with large values of $(k_1 - k_2, (a_2k_1k_2)^\infty)$; since $(k_1 - k_2, k_1k_2) = (k_1 - k_2, v^2)$, we have \[ d_\Delta := (k_1 - k_2, (a_2k_1k_2)^\infty) = (k_1 - k_2, (a_2v)^\infty), \] and the pairs with $d_\Delta > x^\eta$ (as well as $v \le x^{\eta/2}$ and $|k_1 - k_2| > K/x^\eta$) contribute to $\mathcal{S}_1$ at most \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{(m,r)=1} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{k_1 \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2m} \pmod{r} \\ (k_1, re) = 1,\ (k_1, k) = v \\ 0 < |k| \le 8K \\ [d_\Delta, re] \mid k}} |u_{k_1}u_{(k_1+k)}| \\ &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/8} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{(m,r)=1} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{0 < |k| \le 8K \\ [d_\Delta, re] \mid k}} \sum_{\substack{k_1 \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2m} \pmod{r} \\ (k_1, re) = 1,\ (k_1, k) = v}} 1 \\ &\ll x^{\eta/8} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{(m,r)=1} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{0 < |k| \le 8K \\ [d_\Delta, re] \mid k}} \left(\frac{K}{Rv} + 1\right) \\ &\ll x^{\eta/8} \frac{K}{R} \sum_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \frac{1}{v} \sum_{m} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \sum_{\substack{0 < |k| \le 8K \\ d_\Delta \mid k}} \sum_{\substack{e \in \mathscr{E} \\ (r,a_1a_2)=1 \\ re \mid k}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right), \end{aligned} \] using that $Rx^{\eta/2} \ll K$. Bounding the inner sum by $\tau(k)^2 \ll_\eta x^{\eta/9}$, this further becomes \[ \begin{aligned} &\ll_\eta x^{\eta/4} \frac{K}{R} \max_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{m} \frac{1}{M} \Phi\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty \\ d_\Delta \le 8K}} \sum_{\substack{|k| \le 8K \\ d_\Delta \mid k}} 1 \\ &\ll x^{\eta/4} \frac{K}{R} \max_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty \\ d_\Delta \le 8K}} \left(\frac{K}{d_\Delta} + 1 \right) \\ &\ll x^{\eta/4} \frac{K}{R} \max_{v \le x^{\eta/2}} \sum_{\substack{x^\eta < d_\Delta \mid (a_2 v)^\infty \\ d_\Delta \le 8K}} \frac{K}{d_\Delta} \qquad\quad \ll_\eta x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] using the same majorization as in \cref{eq:harmonic-divisors}. The contribution of the pairs with $d_\Delta > x^\eta$ to $\widehat{\Phi}(0) X_1$ is simpler and similarly bounded by $O_\eta(x^{-\eta/4} K^2/R)$. Having eliminated the absolute contribution of all pairs in $\mathcal{K}(\eta)$ at least once, while incurring only admissible errors, this completes our proof of \cref{prop:bad-pairs}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound trivially the contributions of near-diagonal pairs, pairs with large gcd, and pairs with large $b^\infty$-parts, using divisor bounds and a harmonic-divisor majorization.

nodes.name: Reduction to exponential sum
nodes.statement: For $\varepsilon \ge \eta > 0$ and $H := x^\eta R M^{-1}$, under the parameter conditions in \cref{eq:conditions,eq:E-conditions}, one has \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0) X_1 = \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r, a_1a_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1 k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2k_1}}{r} \right) \\ + O_\eta\left(x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R} \right). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: After Poisson summation, $\mathcal S_1-\hat\Phi(0)X_1$ becomes an exponential sum over $1\le|h|\le H$.
conclusions: \mathcal{S}_1 - \widehat{\Phi}(0) X_1 = \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r, a_1a_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1 k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2k_1}}{r} \right) \\ + O_\eta\left(x^{-\eta/4} \frac{K^2}{R} \right). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.label: prop:simplification

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.2
nodes.statement: Rewrite the sum in \cref{prop:bad-pairs} as \[ \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r,a_1a_2)=1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}}\ \mathcal{E}_r(a_1 \overline{a_2 k_1}), \] and apply \cref{lem:poisson} to expand $\mathcal{E}_r(a_1 \overline{a_2 k_1})$. The resulting main term is precisely the sum in \cref{prop:simplification}, while the error terms are acceptable.
nodes.statement_short: Apply truncated Poisson (Lemma 3.4) to the sum from Proposition 8.1.

nodes.name: Why bad pairs are removed before Poisson summation
nodes.statement: The trivial bound for the right-hand side of \cref{prop:simplification} is $H$ times worse than for the right-hand side of \cref{prop:bad-pairs}, due to the additional sum over $h$. This is relevant because $H$ is a nontrivial power of $x$ for the choice of parameters in \cref{eq:optimal-parameters} (where $H \approx R M^{-1} \approx R^2/x$), since we are working with moduli $r$ well-beyond the $\sqrt{x}$ barrier. This is why we needed to eliminate the bad pairs $(k_1, k_2)$ (via \cref{prop:bad-pairs}) \emph{before} applying Poisson summation.

nodes.name: Improved Drappeau-style exponential sum bound
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $\eta \in (0, 1)$, under the parameter conditions in \cref{eq:conditions}, there exists $E$ satisfying \cref{eq:E-conditions} such that the following holds. For any integers $a \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $1 \le b, d_a, d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v, \delta_1, \delta_2 \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ with \[ d_a \mid a, \qquad\quad (d_1, d_2) = (d_1, d_\Delta) = (d_2, d_\Delta) = v, \qquad\quad d_1d_2d_\Delta \mid b^\infty, \] one has \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, b) = 1 \\ r \equiv 0 \pmod{d_a}}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k, n\ell) = 1 \\ (k n \ell, reb) = 1 \\ d_1k - d_2n \ell = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u'_k \beta'_n \gamma'_\ell \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a h \frac{\overline{bk}}{r} \right) \\ \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{O(\eta)-\varepsilon/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] where $H := x^\eta R M^{-1}$, and $|u'_k| \le \tau(d_1 k)$, $|\beta'_n| \le 1$, $|\gamma'_\ell| \le 1$ are sequences supported in $k \asymp K/d_1$, $n \sim N/\delta_1$, and $\ell \sim L/\delta_2$.
nodes.statement_short: A Drappeau-type exponential sum over $e,r,k,n,\ell,h$ is $\ll x^{-\varepsilon}$ times its expected size, for suitable $E$.
assumptions: For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $\eta \in (0, 1)$

For any integers $a \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $1 \le b, d_a, d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v, \delta_1, \delta_2 \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ with \[ d_a \mid a, \qquad\quad (d_1, d_2) = (d_1, d_\Delta) = (d_2, d_\Delta) = v, \qquad\quad d_1d_2d_\Delta \mid b^\infty, \]
where $H := x^\eta R M^{-1}$, and $|u'_k| \le \tau(d_1 k)$, $|\beta'_n| \le 1$, $|\gamma'_\ell| \le 1$ are sequences supported in $k \asymp K/d_1$, $n \sim N/\delta_1$, and $\ell \sim L/\delta_2$.
conclusions: there exists $E$ satisfying \cref{eq:E-conditions} such that the following holds.

one has \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, b) = 1 \\ r \equiv 0 \pmod{d_a}}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k, n\ell) = 1 \\ (k n \ell, reb) = 1 \\ d_1k - d_2n \ell = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u'_k \beta'_n \gamma'_\ell \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a h \frac{\overline{bk}}{r} \right) \\ \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{O(\eta)-\varepsilon/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \]
nodes.label: prop:drappeau-expo

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.2(i) assuming Proposition 8.3
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$ be sufficiently small, and let us pick $E$ as in \cref{prop:drappeau-expo}. By \cref{prop:simplification}, it remains to establish the bound \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_1 := \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r, a_1a_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) \in \mathcal{K}(\eta) \\ (k_1 k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2k_1}}{r} \right) \\ \ll_{\varepsilon,\eta} x^{-2\delta} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{aligned} \] for some choice of $0 < 8\delta \le \eta \le \varepsilon$ in terms of $\varepsilon$ (since $\delta \le \eta/8$, the error term of $x^{-\eta/4} K^2 / R$ from \cref{prop:simplification} is acceptable). For now, let us fix $\delta$ and $\eta$ such that $8\delta \le \eta$; we will give explicit choices at the end of this proof. By the definition of $\mathcal{K}(\eta)$ from \cref{eq:bad-pairs}, we may consider the $x^{\eta}$-bounded variables \[ d_1 := (k_1, (a_2 k_2)^\infty), \qquad d_2 := (k_2, (a_2 k_1)^\infty), \qquad d_\Delta := (k_1 - k_2, (a_2 k_1 k_2)^\infty), \] \begin{equation} v := (k_1, k_2) = (d_1, d_2) = (d_1, d_\Delta) = (d_2, d_\Delta). \end{equation} Noting that $d_1$, $d_2$ and $d_\Delta$ all divide $(a_2 v)^\infty$, we may then expand \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_1 = \sum_{\substack{d_1, d_2, d_\Delta \le x^{\eta} \\ v = (d_1, d_2) = (d_1, d_\Delta) = (d_2, d_\Delta) \\ d_1 d_2 d_\Delta \mid (a_2v)^\infty}} \mathcal{D}_2(d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v), \end{equation} where \[ \mathcal{D}_2 := \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r, a_1 a_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, (a_2 k_2)^\infty) = d_1 \\ (k_2, (a_2 k_1)^\infty) = d_2 \\ (k_1 - k_2, (a_2 k_1 k_2)^\infty) = d_\Delta \\ |k_1 - k_2| > K/x^\eta \\ (k_1 k_2, re) = 1 \\ k_1 \equiv k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{k_1} \overline{u_{k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2 k_1}}{r} \right). \] Changing variables $k_i \mapsto d_i k_i$, this is the same as the sum \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_2 = \sum_{e \in \mathscr{E}} \sum_{(r, a_1 a_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, a_2 d_2 k_2) = 1 \\ (k_2, a_2 d_1 k_1) = 1 \\ (d_1 k_1 - d_2 k_2, (a_2 d_1 d_2 k_1 k_2)^\infty) = d_\Delta \\ |d_1 k_1 - d_2 k_2| > K/x^{\eta} \\ (d_1 k_1 d_2 k_2, re) = 1 \\ d_1 k_1 \equiv d_2 k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{d_1k_1} \overline{u_{d_2k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2d_1k_1}}{r} \right) \\ = \sum_{\substack{e \in \mathscr{E} \\ (e, d_1 d_2) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, a_1 a_2) = 1 \\ (r, d_1 d_2) = 1}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) = 1 \\ (k_1 k_2, re a_2 d_1 d_2) = 1 \\ (d_1 k_1 - d_2 k_2, (a_2 d_1 d_2)^\infty) = d_\Delta \\ |d_1 k_1 - d_2 k_2| > K/x^\eta \\ d_1k_1 \equiv d_2k_2 \pmod{re}}} u_{d_1k_1} \overline{u_{d_2k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a_1 h \frac{\overline{a_2d_1k_1}}{r} \right). \end{aligned} \] Let us denote \[ a := a_1 \textnormal{sgn}(a_2) \qquad\qquad \text{and} \qquad\qquad b := |a_2| d_1 \] for convenience; recalling that $d_2 d_\Delta \mid (a_2 v)^\infty \mid b^\infty$, and that we chose $\mathcal{E} = \{e \sim E : e \text{ prime},\ e \nmid a_2\}$ in \cref{eq:averaging-set}, we further get \[ \mathcal{D}_2 = \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{(r, ab) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) = 1 \\ (k_1 k_2, re b) = 1 \\ d_1k_1 - d_2k_2 = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u_{d_1k_1} \overline{u_{d_2k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a h \frac{\overline{bk_1}}{r} \right). \] At this point we record that, since $a_1, a_2 \ll x^{\delta} \le x^\eta$ by \cref{eq:conditions}, we have \[ d_1 d_2 d_\Delta \mid b^\infty \qquad\qquad \text{and} \qquad\qquad a b d_1 d_2 d_\Delta v \ll x^{O(\eta)}, \] as needed in \cref{prop:drappeau-expo}. We can also get rid of the restriction $(r, a) = 1$ using M\"obius inversion, by writing $\mathbbm{1}_{(r, a) = 1} = \sum_{d_a \mid a} \mu(d_a) \mathbbm{1}_{d_a \mid r}$ and expanding \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_2(d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v) = \sum_{d_a \mid a} \mu(d_a)\, \mathcal{D}_3(d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v, d_a), \end{equation} where \[ \mathcal{D}_3 := \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, b) = 1 \\ r \equiv 0 \pmod{d_a}}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k_1, k_2) = 1 \\ (k_1 k_2, re b) = 1 \\ d_1k_1 - d_2k_2 = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u_{d_1k_1} \overline{u_{d_2k_2}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a h \frac{\overline{bk_1}}{r} \right). \] Finally, using the definition of $(u_k)_k$ from \cref{eq:u-def} and the fact that $(d_2, k_2) = 1$, we can expand \[ u_{d_2 k_2} = \sum_{\delta_1 \delta_2 = d_2} \sum_{n\ell = k_2} \beta_{\delta_1 n} \gamma_{\delta_2 \ell}, \] and thus \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_3(d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v, d_a) = \sum_{\delta_1 \delta_2 = d_2} \mathcal{D}_4(d_1, d_2, d_\Delta, v, d_a, \delta_1), \end{equation} where \[ \mathcal{D}_4 := \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, b) = 1 \\ r \equiv 0 \pmod{d_a}}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k, n\ell) = 1 \\ (k n \ell, re b) = 1 \\ d_1k - d_2n \ell = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u_{d_1k} \overline{\beta_{\delta_1 n} \gamma_{\delta_2 \ell}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(a h \frac{\overline{bk}}{r} \right). \] We can now apply \cref{prop:drappeau-expo} for the sequences \[ u'_k := u_{d_1 k}, \qquad\quad \beta'_n := \overline{\beta_{\delta_1 n}}, \qquad\quad \gamma'_\ell := \overline{\gamma_{\delta_2 \ell}}, \] supported in $k \asymp K/d_1$, $n \sim N/\delta_1$, and $\ell \sim L/\delta_2$ respectively, to get \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_4 \ll_{\eta,\varepsilon} x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/4} \frac{K^2}{R}. \end{equation} Putting together \cref{eq:D12,eq:D23,eq:D34,eq:D4-bound}, we obtain \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_1 \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{d_1,d_2,d_\Delta,v,d_a,\delta_1} \mathcal{D}_4 \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/4} \frac{K^2}{R}, \end{equation} where the supremum includes all applicable restrictions on the tuple $(d_1,d_2,d_\Delta,v,d_a,\delta_1)$ (which takes at most $O_\eta(x^{O(\eta)})$ values). Now let $C > 0$ denote the absolute constant in the final exponent of $O(\eta)$ from \cref{eq:D1-bound}, and let us pick \[ \eta = \eta(\varepsilon) := \min(\varepsilon/(8C), \varepsilon), \qquad\qquad \delta = \delta(\varepsilon) := \min(\varepsilon/16, \eta/8). \] Then we have $0 < 8\delta \le \eta \le \varepsilon$ as desired, and the bound in \cref{eq:D1-bound} implies \[ \mathcal{D}_1 \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{\varepsilon/8 - \varepsilon/4} \frac{K^2}{R} \le x^{-2\delta} \frac{K^2}{R}, \] completing our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize $\mathcal K(\eta)$ by bounded gcd variables, change variables, remove coprimality by Möbius inversion, and apply Proposition 8.3; then choose $\eta,\delta$.

nodes.name: Improved BFI/Maynard exponential sum bound
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $\eta \in (0, 1)$, the following holds. Under the conditions in \cref{eq:conditions}, there exists $E$ satisfying \cref{eq:E-conditions}, such that for any positive integers $b, d$ with $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x^{O(1)}$, and for any parameters $K' \ll NL x^{O(\eta)}$, $N' \asymp N x^{O(\eta)}$, $L' \asymp L x^{O(\eta)}$, $T' \ll NL(RE)^{-1} x^{O(\eta)}$, $H' \ll R M^{-1} x^{O(\eta)}$, one has \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{k \sim K' \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n \sim N' \\ (n, k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{t \sim T' \\ (t, dk) = 1}} t \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \\ (e, dk) = 1}} \sum_{h \sim H'} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L' \\ (\ell, ket) = 1 \\ n \ell \equiv d k \pmod{et}}} \beta(e, h, \ell)\ \textnormal{e}\left(het \frac{\overline{b n \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert^2 \\ \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/2} N^2 L^3, \end{aligned} \end{equation} for any $1$-bounded complex coefficients $\beta(e, h, \ell)$ (independent of $k, n, t$).
nodes.statement_short: A BFI/Maynard-type bilinear exponential sum with Kloosterman fractions saves over $KNL^2$ for suitable $E$.
assumptions: For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $\eta \in (0, 1)$
for any positive integers $b, d$ with $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x^{O(1)}$
for any parameters $K' \ll NL x^{O(\eta)}$, $N' \asymp N x^{O(\eta)}$, $L' \asymp L x^{O(\eta)}$, $T' \ll NL(RE)^{-1} x^{O(\eta)}$, $H' \ll R M^{-1} x^{O(\eta)}$
for any $1$-bounded complex coefficients $\beta(e, h, \ell)$ (independent of $k, n, t$).
conclusions: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{k \sim K' \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n \sim N' \\ (n, k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{t \sim T' \\ (t, dk) = 1}} t \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \\ (e, dk) = 1}} \sum_{h \sim H'} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L' \\ (\ell, ket) = 1 \\ n \ell \equiv d k \pmod{et}}} \beta(e, h, \ell)\ \textnormal{e}\left(het \frac{\overline{b n \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert^2 \\ \ll_{\varepsilon, \eta} x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/2} N^2 L^3, \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.label: prop:bfi-expo

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.3 assuming Proposition 8.4
nodes.statement: Let us denote the sum in \cref{prop:drappeau-expo} by $\mathcal{D}_4$, and assume without loss of generality that $(d_a, b) = 1$ (since otherwise $\mathcal{D}_4$ vanishes). We choose $E$ as in \cref{prop:bfi-expo}, and take a closer look at the exponential: by iterating \cref{lem:bezout}, since $b, k, r$ are pairwise coprime we have \[ \frac{\overline{bk}}{r} + \frac{\overline{rb}}{k} + \frac{\overline{rk}}{b} \equiv \frac{1}{bkr} \quad \pmod{1}, \] and thus, using that $re d_\Delta t \equiv d_2 n \ell \pmod{k}$, \[ ah\frac{\overline{b k}}{r} \equiv - ah e d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n\ell}}{k} - ah\frac{\overline{rk}}{b} + \frac{ah}{b k r} \quad \pmod{1}. \] Since $|a| \ll x^\eta$, $h \ll x^\eta R M^{-1}$, $kr \gg KR/x^\eta$ and $KM \asymp x$, we obtain \[ \textnormal{e}\left(ah \frac{\overline{b k}}{r} \right) = \textnormal{e}\left(- ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k} - ah\frac{\overline{rk}}{b} \right) + O(x^{3\eta-1}), \] and thus \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_4 = &\sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(r, b) = 1 \\ r \equiv 0 \pmod{d_a}}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} \sum_{\substack{(k, n\ell) = 1 \\ (k n \ell, reb) = 1 \\ d_1k - d_2n \ell = red_\Delta t \\ (t, b) = 1,\ red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta}} u'_k \beta'_n \gamma'_\ell \\ &\times \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(- ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k} - ah\frac{\overline{rk}}{b} \right) + O\left(E\frac{R}{R}NL \left(\frac{K}{RE} + 1\right) H x^{3\eta - 1} \right). \end{aligned} \] Recalling that $K \gg RE$ (due to \cref{eq:E-conditions}), $H = x^\eta RM^{-1}$ and $MK \asymp x$, the error term is \[ \ll \frac{EK^2 H x^{3\eta - 1}}{RE} \ll K^3 x^{4\eta - 2} \ll x^{O(\eta)-\varepsilon} \frac{K^2}{R}, \] which is acceptable (the final bound $KR \ll x^{2-\varepsilon}$ follows from \cref{eq:conditions}). We change variables by replacing the $r$-summation with a summation over \[ t := \frac{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell}{red_\Delta}, \] noting that the condition $red_\Delta |t| > K/x^\eta$ implies $|t| > K/(6RE x^{2\eta})$. We also put $|t|$ into dyadic intervals $|t| \sim T$ to obtain \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_4 \ll \sum_{\substack{T = 2^j \\ K/(RE x^{2\eta}) \ll T \ll K/RE}} \mathcal{D}_5(T) + O\left(x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon} \frac{K^2}{R}\right), \end{equation} where \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_5 := \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{|t| \sim T \\ (t, b) = 1}}\, \sum_{\substack{(k, n\ell) = (k n \ell, d_aebt) = 1 \\ d_1k \equiv d_2n \ell \pmod{d_aed_\Delta t} \\ |d_1k - d_2n \ell| > K/x^\eta \\ r := (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell)/(ed_\Delta t) \\ (r, b) = 1}} &\Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} u'_k \beta'_n \gamma'_\ell \\ &\times \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{-hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k} + ah\frac{\overline{rk}}{b} \right). \end{aligned} \] (We inserted the condition $(kn\ell, t) = 1$; this must happen since $t \mid d_1 k - d_2 n \ell$ and $(t, d_1 d_2) \mid (t, b^\infty) = 1$; if a prime divides both $t$ and one of $k$ and $n\ell$, then it must also divide the other, contradicting $(k, n\ell) = 1$. Moreover, the conditions in the sum over $k, n, \ell$ are enough to imply $(kn\ell, r) = 1$, since $(d_1 k - d_2 n\ell, k) = (d_2 n\ell, k) = (d_2, k) \mid (b^\infty, k) = 1$ and similarly $(d_1 k- d_2 n\ell, n\ell) = 1$.) We now aim to simplify the term $ah \overline{rk}/b$ from the exponential, by fixing all relevant residues modulo $b$. With this goal, we denote the residues of $e, t$ modulo $b$ by $\widehat{e}, \widehat{t}$, and those of $k, n, \ell$ modulo $d_\Delta b$ by $\widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell}$. Since $(d_1 k - d_2n\ell)/d_\Delta = ret$ is coprime with $b$, we must have $d_1 \widehat{k} - d_2 \widehat{n} \widehat{\ell} \in d_\Delta (\mathbf{Z}/b\mathbf{Z})^\times$ $= \{d_\Delta n + d_\Delta b \mathbf{Z} : (n, b) = 1\}$ (viewed as a subset of $\mathbf{Z}/d_\Delta b \mathbf{Z}$). This allows us to expand $\mathcal{D}_5$ as \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_5(T) = \sum_{\substack{\widehat{e}, \widehat{t} \in (\mathbf{Z}/b\mathbf{Z})^\times}} \sum_{\substack{\widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell} \in \mathbf{Z}/d_\Delta b\mathbf{Z} \\ (\widehat{k} \widehat{n} \widehat{\ell}, b) = 1 \\ d_1 \widehat{k} - d_2 \widehat{n} \widehat{\ell} \in d_\Delta (\mathbf{Z}/b\mathbf{Z})^\times}} \mathcal{D}_6\left(T, \widehat{e}, \widehat{t}, \widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell}\right), \end{equation} with \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_6 := \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ e \equiv \widehat{e} \pmod{b}}} \sum_{\substack{|t| \sim T \\ t \equiv \widehat{t} \pmod{b}}}\, &\sum_{\substack{(k, n, \ell) \equiv (\widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell}) \pmod{d_\Delta b} \\ (k, n\ell) = (k n \ell, d_aet) = 1 \\ d_1k \equiv d_2n \ell \pmod{d_aed_\Delta t} \\ |d_1k - d_2n \ell| > K/x^\eta \\ r := (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell)/(ed_\Delta t)}} \Phi\left(\frac{r}{R}\right) \frac{1}{r} u'_k \beta'_n \gamma'_\ell \\ &\times \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{-hM}{r}\right) \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k} + ah\frac{\overline{\widehat{r}\widehat{k}}}{b} \right), \end{aligned} \] where $\widehat{r} = \widehat{r}(\widehat{e}, \widehat{t}, \widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell}) \in (\mathbf{Z}/b\mathbf{Z})^\times$ is the unique residue mod $b$ such that $d_\Delta \widehat{r} \widehat{e} \widehat{t} = d_1 \widehat{k} - d_2 \widehat{n} \widehat{\ell} \in \mathbf{Z}/d_\Delta b \mathbf{Z}$ (this $\widehat{r}$ is the residue of $r$ mod $b$, and it is fixed inside each $\mathcal{D}_6$). Denoting $y(h) := \textnormal{e}\left( ah\overline{\widehat{r} \widehat{k}}/b \right)$ and suppressing the congruences to $\widehat{e}, \widehat{t}, \widehat{k}, \widehat{n}, \widehat{\ell}$ through the notation $\sum^*$, we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}_6 = \sum^*_{\substack{|t| \sim T \\ (t, b) = 1}} \sum^*_{\substack{(k, n) = 1 \\ (kn, d_abt) = 1}} u'_k \beta'_n \sum^*_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ (e, knb) = 1}} \sum^*_{\substack{(\ell, d_aekbt) = 1 \\ d_2 n \ell \equiv d_1 k \pmod{d_aed_\Delta t} \\ |d_2 n \ell - d_1 k | > K/x^\eta}} \sum_{1 \le |h| \le H} \gamma'_\ell\ y(h)\ \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k}\right) \\ \times \left[ \Phi \left(\frac{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell}{ed_\Delta tR} \right) \frac{e d_\Delta t}{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{- h e d_\Delta t M}{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell}\right) \right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We now remove some of the dependencies between the variables $t, k, n$ and $e, \ell, h$, as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.4]{maynard2020primes}. Consider the function \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi(e, \ell, h) &:= \Phi \left(\frac{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell}{ed_\Delta tR} \right) \frac{e d_\Delta t}{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell} \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{-h e d_\Delta t M}{d_1 k - d_2 n \ell}\right) = \frac{1}{R} \alpha\, \Phi\left(\frac{1}{\alpha}\right) \widehat{\Phi}\left(\frac{-Mh}{R} \alpha \right), \end{aligned} \] where $\alpha := e d_\Delta t R / (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell)$; note that $\Psi$ is smooth in $e, \ell, h$, and nonzero only if $\alpha \asymp 1$. Since $Mh/R \ll x^\eta$ and $\Phi$, $\widehat{\Phi}$ have bounded derivatives, the chain rule implies the bounds \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial^{j_1 + j_2 + j_3}}{(\partial e)^{j_1} (\partial (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell))^{j_2} (\partial h)^{j_3}}\Psi(e, \ell, h) &\ll_{j_1, j_2, j_3} \frac{x^{\eta(j_1 + j_2 + j_3)}}{R} |e|^{-j_1} |d_1 k - d_2 n \ell|^{-j_2} |h|^{-j_3} \\ &\ll \frac{x^{\eta(j_1 + 2j_2 + j_3)}}{R} |e|^{-j_1} |d_2 n \ell|^{-j_2} |h|^{-j_3}, \end{aligned} \] where we used that $d_2 n \ell \asymp K$ and $|d_2 n \ell - d_1 k| > K/x^\eta$ in the last line. We thus have \[ \frac{\partial^{j_1 + j_2 + j_3}}{(\partial e)^{j_1} (\partial \ell)^{j_2} (\partial h)^{j_3}}\Psi(e, \ell, h) \ll_{j_1, j_2, j_3} \frac{x^{\eta(j_1 + 2j_2 + j_3)}}{R} |e|^{-j_1} |\ell|^{-j_2} |h|^{-j_3}, \] and then by partial summation, \cref{eq:before-partial} implies that \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_6 \ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)}}{R} \sup_{\substack{H'' \le H \\ E'' \le 2E,\ L'' \le 2L}} \mathcal{D}_7, \end{equation} where \[ \mathcal{D}_7 := \sum_{\substack{|t| \sim T \\ (t, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{(k, n) = 1 \\ (kn, d_abt) = 1}} |u'_k \beta'_n| \left\vert \sum^*_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ e \le E'' \\ (e, knb) = 1}} \sum^*_{\substack{(\ell, d_aekbt) = 1,\ \ell \le L'' \\ d_2 n \ell \equiv d_1 k \pmod{d_aed_\Delta t} \\ |d_2 n \ell - d_1 k| > K/x^\eta \\ (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell)/t > 0}} \gamma'_\ell \sum_{|h| \sim H''} y(h)\ \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert. \] (We removed the residue constraints in the outer sums over $t, k, n$ for an upper bound and we put $|h|$ into a dyadic interval, losing only a logarithmic factor.) According to the desired bound in \cref{prop:drappeau-expo}, and in light of \cref{eq:D45,eq:D56,eq:D67}, it remains to show that \begin{equation} \mathcal{D}_7 \ll_{\varepsilon,\eta} x^{O(\eta)-\varepsilon/4} K^2, \end{equation} for all $\eta \in (0, 1)$. Now let $\mathcal{I}(t, k, n)$ be the subinterval of $[L/\delta_2, 2L/\delta_2]$ (which is the support of $\gamma'_\ell$) containing those $\ell$'s such that \[ \ell \le L'', \qquad |d_2 n \ell - d_1 k| > K/x^\eta, \qquad \text{and} \qquad (d_1 k - d_2 n \ell)/t > 0. \] As in the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.4]{maynard2020primes}, we can remove the constraint $\ell \in \mathcal{I}(t, k, n)$ using the identity \[ \mathbbm{1}_{\ell \in \mathcal{I}(t, k, n)} = \int_0^1 \textnormal{e}(\ell \omega) \sum_{j \in \mathcal{I}(t, k, n)} \textnormal{e}(-j\omega)\, d\omega = \int_0^1 \textnormal{e}(\ell \omega) c(t, k, n, \omega)\min(L, \omega^{-1} (1 - \omega)^{-1}) \,d\omega, \] for some coefficients $c(t, k, n, \omega) \ll 1$, and the $L^1$ bound $\int_0^{1/2} \min(L, 2\omega^{-1}) d\omega \ll \log x$. Together with the divisor bound $|u'_k| \ll_\eta x^\eta$, this shows that \[ \mathcal{D}_7 \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{\omega \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{D}_8, \] where \[ \mathcal{D}_8 := \sum_{\substack{|t| \sim T \\ (t, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{k \asymp K/d_1,\ n \sim N/\delta_1 \\ (k, n) = 1 \\ (kn, d_abt) = 1}} \left\vert \sum^*_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ e \le E'' \\ (e, knb) = 1}} \sum^*_{\substack{(\ell, d_aekbt) = 1 \\ d_2 n \ell \equiv d_1 k \pmod{d_aed_\Delta t}}} \gamma'_\ell\, \textnormal{e}(\ell \omega) \sum_{|h| \sim H''} y(h)\ \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta t \frac{\overline{b d_2n \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert. \] We denote $d_i' := d_i/v$ for $i \in \{1, 2, \Delta\}$, so that the exponential term and the congruence in the summation over $\ell$ may be rewritten as \[ \textnormal{e}\left(ahe d_\Delta' t \frac{\overline{b d_2' n \ell}}{k}\right), \qquad\qquad d_2' n \ell \equiv d_1' k \pmod{e d_a d_\Delta' t}, \] where $(d_1', d_2') = (d_1', d_\Delta') = (d_2', d_\Delta') = 1$. At this point, it also makes sense to denote \[ h' := \frac{a}{d_a} h, \qquad\qquad t' := d_a d_\Delta' t, \qquad\qquad n' := d_2' n, \] \[ H' := \frac{a}{d_a}H'', \qquad\qquad T' := d_a d_\Delta' T, \qquad\qquad N' := \frac{d_2'}{\delta_1}N, \qquad\qquad L' := \frac{L}{\delta_2}, \qquad\qquad K' := \frac{K}{d_1}, \] to bound \[ \mathcal{D}_8 \ll \sum_{\substack{k \asymp K' \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n' \sim N' \\ (n', k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{|t'| \sim T' \\ (t', d_1'k) = 1}} \left\vert \sum^*_{\substack{e \sim E \text{ prime} \\ e \le E'' \\ (e, kn'b) = 1}} \sum^*_{\substack{\ell \sim L' \\ (\ell, bket') = 1 \\ n' \ell \equiv d_1' k \pmod{et'}}} \gamma'_\ell\, \textnormal{e}(\ell \omega) \sum_{\substack{|h'| \sim H' \\ a/d_a \mid h'}} y(h'd_a/a)\ \textnormal{e}\left(h' e t' \frac{\overline{b n' \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert. \] (To verify the new GCD constraints, recall that $(d_a, b) = 1$ and $d_1' d_2' d_\Delta' \mid b^\infty$.) We may replace the restriction that $(e, n') = 1$ with $(e, d_1') = 1$, since each follows from the other and the congruence $n'\ell \equiv d_1' k \pmod{e}$, where $(\ell k, e) = 1$. Moreover, by inserting $1$-bounded coefficients $\beta(e, h', \ell)$, we can get rid of the coefficients $\gamma'_\ell\, \textnormal{e}(\ell\omega) y(h'd_a/a)$, the residue constraints (modulo $b$) in the summations over $e$ and $\ell$, as well as of the constraints that $e$ is a prime and $e \le E'$, and that $a/d_a \mid h'$. Overall, this yields \[ \mathcal{D}_8 \ll \sum_{\substack{k \asymp K' \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n' \sim N' \\ (n', k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{|t'| \sim T' \\ (t', d_1'k) = 1}} \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \\ (e, d_1'k) = 1}} \sum_{|h'| \sim H'} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L' \\ (\ell, ket') = 1 \\ n' \ell \equiv d_1' k \pmod{et'}}} \beta(e, h', \ell)\, \textnormal{e}\left(h' e t' \frac{\overline{b n' \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert. \] Finally, we insert a factor of $\sqrt{|t'|/T'}$ into the sum, and apply Cauchy--Schwarz in the outer variables $k, n', t'$ to bound \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathcal{D}_8^2 \ll \\ &K' N' \sum_{\substack{k \asymp K' \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n' \sim N' \\ (n', k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{|t'| \sim T' \\ (t', d_1' k) = 1}} |t'| \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \\ (e, d_1'k) = 1}} \sum_{|h'| \sim H'} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L' \\ (\ell, ket') = 1 \\ n' \ell \equiv d_1' k \pmod{et'}}} \beta(e, h', \ell)\, \textnormal{e}\left(h' e t' \frac{\overline{b n' \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert^2. \end{aligned} \] Conjugating if necessary when $h' < 0$ or $t' < 0$, \cref{prop:bfi-expo} implies that \[ \mathcal{D}_8^2 \ll_{\varepsilon,\eta} K'N' \cdot x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/2} K N L^2, \] for all $\eta \in (0, 1)$. Putting things together, we conclude that \[ \mathcal{D}_7 \ll_{\varepsilon,\eta} x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{\omega \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{D}_8 \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/4} \sqrt{K^2N^2L^2} \asymp x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon/4} K^2, \] as we required in \cref{eq:B-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the phase via Bézout, substitute $t=(d_1k-d_2n\ell)/(red_\Delta)$, fix residues mod $b$, separate variables by partial summation, then Cauchy–Schwarz and Proposition 8.4.

nodes.name: General BFI-style sum $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement: To aid future research, we shall consider a general sum \[ \mathcal{B}(K, N, T, E, H, L) := \sum_{\substack{k \sim K \\ (k, b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{n \sim N \\ (n, k) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \\ (t, dk) = 1}} t \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \\ (e, dk) = 1}} \sum_{h \sim H} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L \\ (\ell, ket) = 1 \\ n \ell \equiv d k \pmod{et}}} \beta(e, h, \ell)\ \textnormal{e}\left(het \frac{\overline{b n \ell}}{k}\right) \right\vert^2, \] where $b, d$ are given positive integers with $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x$, $\beta(e, h, \ell)$ are arbitrary $1$-bounded coefficients, and the parameters $K, N, T, E, H, L$ are almost arbitrary.
nodes.statement_short: A general bilinear exponential sum $\mathcal B$ with phases $e(dh\bar{b\ell}\ldots)$ and arbitrary coefficients $\beta(e,h,\ell)$.

nodes.name: Trivial bound for $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement: The trivial bound for $\mathcal{B}$ is $KN\left(TEH\left(\frac{L}{ET} + 1\right)\right)^2 \ll KN(HL)^2 + KN(TEH)^2$, but we need more than a power saving over this (note that the desired bound in \cref{eq:bfi-expo} is on the order of $KNL^2$, since we need to make up for the factors of $H$ introduced during Poisson summation). So the relative sizes of $K, N, T, E, H, L$ (as given by \cref{prop:bfi-expo} and \cref{eq:conditions}) will ultimately be crucial, although we only take them into account after proving a general bound in \cref{prop:bfi-expo-2}.

nodes.name: Splitting the BFI-style sum
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal B$ is bounded by diagonal and zero-frequency terms plus sums $\mathcal B_=$, $\mathcal B_{\neq}$ of Kloosterman sums with $\ell_1=\ell_2$ and $\ell_1\ne\ell_2$.
assumptions: For $\eta \in (0, 1)$, $1 \ll K, N, T, E, H, L \ll x$
any positive integers $b, d$ with $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x$
conclusions: \mathcal{B}(K, N, T, E, H, L) \ll_\eta\ & x^{O(\eta)} \Bigg( KNTHL + KEHT^2L + N H^2 L^2 + N H^2 T L \\ &+ \frac{N}{KE^2} \sup_{\substack{E_0 \ll E,\ S \ll TE_0, \\ J \ll (K T E^2 x^\eta)/(NE_0) \\ w \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z},\, g_0}} E_0\, (\mathcal{B}_= + \mathcal{B}_{\neq}) \Bigg), \end{aligned} \]
nodes.label: lem:splitting-bfi

nodes.name: Origin of the terms in Lemma 9.1
nodes.statement: After expanding the square inside $\mathcal{B}$, the `diagonal terms' with $h_1 e_1 \ell_2 = h_2 e_2 \ell_1$ bring a contribution of roughly $O(KNTHL + KEHT^2L)$; handling this will require our deamplification setup with $E > 1$. Among the off-diagonal terms, a contribution of $O(NH^2L^2 + NH^2TL)$ comes from the zeroth Fourier coefficient in a completion of Kloosterman sums (via \cref{lem:completion}). The remaining terms are ultimately separated into $\mathcal{B}_=$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\neq}$, depending on whether $\ell_1 = \ell_2$ or $\ell_1 \neq \ell_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.1
nodes.statement:
This is essentially the same as the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.5]{maynard2020primes}, but in a slightly more general setting (the main difference being the additional parameters $b, d$). We first replace the indicator functions of $k \sim K$ and $n \sim N$ with smooth majorants, using a suitable smooth compactly supported function $f_0$ (we choose this as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.5]{maynard2020primes}). Expanding out the square in $\mathcal{B}$ and swapping sums, we then obtain  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B} &\le \sum_{\substack{k \ (k, b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight) \sum_{\substack{n \ (n, k) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, dk) = 1}} t \left\vert \sum_{\substack{e \sim E \ (e, dk) = 1}} \sum_{h \sim H} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L \ (\ell, ket) = 1 \ n \ell \equiv d k \pmod{et}}}  eta(e, h, \ell)\ 	extnormal{e}\left(het  rac{\overline{b n \ell}}{k}ight) ight\vert^2 \ &= \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} t \sum_{\substack{e_1, e_2 \sim E \ (e_1 e_2, d) = 1}}\ \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{t(e_1, e_2)} \ (\ell_1, te_1) = 1 \ (\ell_2, te_2) = 1}} \sum_{h_1, h_2 \sim H}  eta(e_1, h_1, \ell_1) \, \overline{ eta(e_2, h_2, \ell_2)} \ &\qquad\qquad 	imes \sum_{\substack{k \ (k, te_1e_2\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight) \sum_{\substack{(n, k) = 1 \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_1} \pmod{te_1} \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_2} \pmod{te_2}}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) 	extnormal{e} \left(t rac{(h_1e_1\ell_2 - h_2e_2\ell_1)\overline{bn \ell_1 \ell_2}}{k} ight), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where we used that $(n, et) = 1$ to deduce the congruence between $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ (indeed, if a prime $p$ divided both $n$ and $et$, then it would divide $dk$, but $(et, dk) = 1$). Let $\mathcal{B}_1$ denote the contribution of the `diagonal' terms with $h_1 e_1 \ell_2 = h_2 e_2 \ell_1$, and $\mathcal{B}_2$ contain the other terms; thus we have $\mathcal{B} \le \mathcal{B}_1 + \mathcal{B}_2$. We first bound $\mathcal{B}_1$ trivially (using the divisor bound) by  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_1 &\ll \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} t \sum_{\substack{e_1 \sim E \ \ell_2 \sim L \ h_1 \sim H}} \, \sum_{\substack{e_2 \sim E \ \ell_1 \sim L \ e_2\ell_1 \mid h_1e_1\ell_2 \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{t(e_1,e_2)} \ (\ell_1, te_1) = (\ell_2, te_2) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1\ell_2 = h_2e_2\ell_1}} \sum_k f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight) \sum_{\substack{n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_1} \pmod{te_1} \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_2} \pmod{te_2}}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) \ &\ll \sum_{t \sim T} t \sum_{\substack{e_1 \sim E \ \ell_2 \sim L \ h_1 \sim H}} \, \sum_{\substack{e_2 \sim E,\ \ell_1 \sim L \ h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1\ell_2 = h_2e_2\ell_1 \ (\ell_1, te_1) = 1}} \sum_{k \ll K} \sum_{\substack{n \ll N \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_1} \pmod{te_1}}} 1 \ &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)}\, T^2 ELHK \left( rac{N}{TE} + 1ight), \end{aligned} \end{equation} recovering the first two terms in the desired bound. Next, we consider $\mathcal{B}_2$, containing the terms with $h_1 e_1 \ell_2 
eq h_2 e_2 \ell_1$. We let $e_0 := (e_1, e_2)$, $e_1' := e_1/e_0$ and $e_2' := e_2/e_0$ and put $e_0$ in dyadic ranges $e_0 \sim E_0$ to write \[  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_2 &\ll (\log x) \ &	imes \sup_{E_0 \ll E}  igg\vert \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} t \sum_{\substack{e_0 \sim E_0 \ (e_0, d) = 1}}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \ (e_1', e_2') = 1 \ (e_1' e_2', d) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0} \ (\ell_1 \ell_2, te_0) = 1 \ (\ell_1, e_1') = (\ell_2, e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1'\ell_2 
eq h_2e_2'\ell_1}}  eta(e_0e_1', h_1, \ell_1) \, \overline{ eta(e_0e_2', h_2, \ell_2)} \ &	imes \sum_{\substack{k \ (k, te_0e_1'e_2'\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight) \sum_{\substack{(n, k) = 1 \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_1} \pmod{te_0e_1'} \ n \equiv dk\overline{\ell_2} \pmod{te_0e_2'}}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) 	extnormal{e} \left(te_0 rac{(h_1e_1'\ell_2 - h_2e_2'\ell_1)\overline{bn \ell_1 \ell_2}}{k} ight) igg\vert. \end{aligned} \] Note that the inner sum over $n$ can be rewritten as \[ \sum_{\substack{n \equiv k\mu \pmod{te_0e_1'e_2'} \ (n, k) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) 	extnormal{e} \left( rac{\overline{n}r_0}{k} ight), \] where $r_0 := te_0 (h_1e_1'\ell_2 - h_2e_2'\ell_1)\overline{b \ell_1 \ell_2}$ (defined mod $k$), and $\mu = \mu(\ell_1, \ell_2, t, e_0, e_1', e_2', d)$ is the unique solution (mod $te_0e_1'e_2'$) to the congruences $\mu \equiv d\overline{\ell_1} \pmod{te_0e_1'}$ and $\mu \equiv d\overline{\ell_2} \pmod{te_0e_2'}$; the latter is well-defined by the Chinese Remainder Theorem, since $(te_0e_1', te_0e_2') = te_0(e_1', e_2') = te_0$, $[te_0e_1', te_0e_2'] = te_0e_1'e_2'$, and $d\overline{\ell_1} \equiv d\overline{\ell_2} \pmod{te_0}$. Crucially, note that $\mu$ does not depend on $k$. We can thus complete Kloosterman sums using \cref{lem:completion}, with  egin{gather*} q := te_0e_1'e_2', \ J_0 := 32\, x^\eta  rac{KTE^2}{NE_0} \ge x^\eta  rac{kq}{N}, \end{gather*} giving us \[  egin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{n \equiv k\mu \pmod{q} \ (n, k) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{n}{N}ight) 	extnormal{e}\left( rac{\overline{n}r_0}{k}ight) &=  rac{N}{kq} \sum_{|j| \le J_0} \widehat{f_0}\left( rac{jN}{kq}ight) 	extnormal{e}\left( rac{j\mu}{q}ight) S(j\overline{q}, r_0; k) + O_{\eta}\left(x^{-100}ight) \ &=  rac{N}{kq} \sum_{|j| \le J_0} \widehat{f_0}\left( rac{jN}{kq}ight) 	extnormal{e}\left( rac{j\mu}{q}ight) S(r_1, j; k) + O_{\eta}\left(x^{-100}ight), \end{aligned} \] where \[ r_1 := r_0 \overline{q} = (h_1e_1'\ell_2 - h_2e_2'\ell_1)\, \overline{b \ell_1 \ell_2 e_1' e_2'}. \] We now plug this bound into our estimate for $\mathcal{B}_2$, isolate the contribution of $j = 0$ into $\mathcal{B}_3$, and let $\mathcal{B}_4$ contain the terms with $j 
eq 0$. This yields  egin{equation} \mathcal{B}_2 \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{E_0 \ll E} (|\mathcal{B}_3| + |\mathcal{B}_4|) + O_\eta(x^{-50}), \end{equation} where \[  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_3 := \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} t \sum_{\substack{e_0 \sim E_0 \ (e_0, d) = 1}}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \ (e_1', e_2') = 1 \ (e_1' e_2', d) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0} \ (\ell_1 \ell_2, te_0) = 1 \ (\ell_1, e_1') = (\ell_2, e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1'\ell_2 
eq h_2e_2'\ell_1}}  eta(e_0e_1', h_1, \ell_1) \, \overline{ eta(e_0e_2', h_2, \ell_2)} \ \qquad\qquad 	imes \sum_{\substack{k \ (k, te_0e_1'e_2'\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight)  rac{N}{kq} \widehat{f_0}\left(0ight) S(r_1, 0; k), \end{aligned} \] \[  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_4 := \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} t \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_0 \sim E_0 \ (e_0, d) = 1}}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \ (e_1', e_2') = 1 \ (e_1' e_2', d) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0} \ (\ell_1 \ell_2, te_0) = 1 \ (\ell_1, e_1') = (\ell_2, e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1'\ell_2 
eq h_2e_2'\ell_1}}  eta(e_0e_1', h_1, \ell_1) \, \overline{ eta(e_0e_2', h_2, \ell_2)} \ \qquad\qquad 	imes \sum_{\substack{k \ (k, te_0e_1'e_2'\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k}{K}ight)  rac{N}{kq} \sum_{\substack{|j| \le J_0 \ j 
eq 0}} \widehat{f_0}\left( rac{jN}{kq}ight) 	extnormal{e}\left( rac{j\mu}{q}ight) S(r_1, j; k). \end{aligned} \] We bound $\mathcal{B}_3$ trivially using the Weil bound (\cref{lem:weil}):  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_3 &\ll \sum_{t \sim T} t \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0}}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H}} \sum_{k \ll K}  rac{N}{kq} (r_1, k) \ &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sum_{t \sim T} t \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0}}}\,  rac{H^2N}{q} \ &\ll x^{O(\eta)}\, T^2  rac{E^2}{E_0} L\left(1 +  rac{L}{TE_0}ight)  rac{H^2NE_0}{TE^2} \ &\ll x^{O(\eta)} \left(TLH^2N + L^2H^2N ight), \end{aligned} \end{equation} giving the third and fourth terms in the desired bound. We finally turn to estimating $\mathcal{B}_4$, and start by removing the coprimality constraint $(k, te_0) = 1$, via M"obius inversion. We write $\mathbbm{1}_{(k, te_0) = 1} = \sum_{s \mid (k, te_0)} \mu(s)$ and $k = k' s$, and put $j, s$ into dyadic ranges $j \sim J, s \sim S$ to obtain  egin{equation} \mathcal{B}_4 \ll_\eta x^\eta T \sup_{\substack{S \ll TE_0 \ J \ll J_0}} \mathcal{B}_5, \end{equation} where  egin{equation} \mathcal{B}_5 := \sum_{\substack{t \sim T \ (t, d) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{e_0 \sim E_0 \ (e_0, d) = 1}}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \ (e_1', e_2') = 1 \ (e_1' e_2', d) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \ s \mid te_0 \ (s, e_1'e_2'b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0} \ (\ell_1 \ell_2, te_0) = 1 \ (\ell_1, e_1') = (\ell_2, e_2') = 1}} \mathcal{B}_6, \end{equation} \[ \mathcal{B}_6 := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1'\ell_2 
eq h_2e_2'\ell_1}} \left\vert \sum_{\substack{k' \ (k', e_1'e_2'\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} f_0\left( rac{k's}{K}ight)  rac{N}{k'sq} \sum_{j \sim J} \widehat{f_0}\left( rac{jN}{k'sq}ight) 	extnormal{e}\left( rac{j\mu}{q}ight) S(r_1, j; k's) ight\vert. \] We now wish to separate the $j, k'$ variables in $\mathcal{B}_6$ from the others, in the factors of $f_0$, $\widehat{f_0}$, and the exponential term; note that $s$, $q = te_0e_1'e_2'$ and $\mu = \mu(\ell_1, \ell_2, c, t, e_0, e_1', e_2', d)$ do not depend on $j$ and $k'$. As in the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.5]{maynard2020primes}, we make use of the special choice of the smooth function $f_0(t) := \int_0^\infty \psi_0(y) \psi_0(t/y)\, dy/y$ (which is a multiplicative convolution of a bounded smooth function $\psi_0$ supported on $[1/2, 5/2]$ with itself) to find that \[ f_0\left( rac{k's}{K}ight) = \int_U^{20U} \psi_0(su)\, \psi_0\left( rac{k'}{Ku}ight)  rac{du}{u}, \] where $U \asymp 1/S$, and also \[  rac{N}{k'sq}\widehat{f_0} \left(  rac{jN}{k'sq} ight) = \int_V^{20V} \int_W^{20W} \psi_0(k'v)\, \psi_0\left( rac{wsq}{Nv} ight) 	extnormal{e}(-jw)\, dw  rac{dv}{v}, \] where $V \asymp S/K$ and $W \asymp NVE_0/(STE^2) \asymp NE_0/(KTE^2)$. Plugging this into our expression for $\mathcal{B}_6$, taking the integrals over $u, v, w$ outside the absolute value by the triangle inequality, and swapping them with the sum over $h_1, h_2$, we get  egin{equation} \mathcal{B}_6 \ll \int_U^{20 U} \int_V^{20 V} \int_W^{20 W} |\mathcal{B}_7|  rac{du\, dv\, dw}{uv}, \end{equation} where \[ \mathcal{B}_7 := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \ h_1e_1'\ell_2 
eq h_2e_2'\ell_1}} \left\vert \sum_{\substack{k' \ (k', e_1'e_2'\ell_1\ell_2b) = 1}} g_{u,v} \left( rac{k'}{K/S}ight) \sum_{|j| \sim J} 	extnormal{e}\left(j \left( rac{\mu}{q} - wight)ight)\, S(r_1, j; k's) ight\vert, \] and the smooth function \[ g_{u,v}(t) := \psi_0\left( rac{t}{uS}ight) \psi_0\left( rac{vtK}{S}ight) \] is supported on $t \asymp 1$. Combining this with \cref{eq:b4-estimate,eq:b5-estimate,eq:b6-estimate}, moving the integrals in $u, v, w$ to the front and taking an $L^\infty$ bound, we find that \[ \mathcal{B}_4 \ll_\eta x^{\eta} TW \sup_{\substack{S \ll TE_0 \ J \ll J_0}} \sup_{\substack{u \asymp 1/S \ v \asymp S/K \ w \asymp NE_0/KE^2}} \sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \ s \mid te_0 \ (s, e_1'e_2'b) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{\ell_1, \ell_2 \sim L \ \ell_1 \equiv \ell_2 \pmod{te_0} \ (\ell_1 \ell_2, te_0) = 1 \ (\ell_1, e_1') = (\ell_2, e_2') = 1}} \mathcal{B}_7, \] where $TW \asymp  rac{NE_0}{KE^2}$. Letting $\mathcal{B}_=$ be the contribution of the terms $\ell_1 = \ell_2$ and $\mathcal{B}_{
eq}$ contain the terms with $\ell_1 
eq \ell_2$, and combining this with \cref{eq:b-estimate,eq:b1-estimate,eq:b2-estimate,eq:b3-estimate}, we recover the desired bound for $\mathcal{B}$ (note that when $\ell_1 = \ell_2 = \ell$, one can take $\mu = d\overline{\ell}$).
nodes.statement_short: Expand the square, bound diagonal terms trivially, complete Kloosterman sums (Lemma 3.5), bound $j=0$ by Weil, and separate variables via a multiplicative-convolution smooth weight.

nodes.name: Contribution of $\ell_1 = \ell_2$
nodes.statement: With the notation of \cref{lem:splitting-bfi}, assuming that $EHT \ll x^{O(\eta)} KNL$, one has \[ \mathcal{B}_= \ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)} K E^2}{NE_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{E^2L}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(KT^5E^8H^2L^3 N\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{H}{E} + \frac{H^2}{E^2L}\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL} \right)^{1/2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound for $\mathcal B_=$ via the DI-type Kloosterman bound.
nodes.label: lem:split-bfi-eq

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.2 assuming Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement: Here we adapt the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.7]{maynard2020primes}, using \cref{thm:di-type-bound} instead of \cite[Theorem 9]{deshouillers1982kloosterman}. To do this, we need to eliminate the dependency of the inner exponential coefficients on $\ell$, so we write \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &= \sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \\ s \mid te_0 \\ (s, e_1'e_2'b) = 1}} \sum_{\widehat{\ell} \in (\mathbf{Z}/te_0e_1'e_2'\mathbf{Z})^\times} \sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L \\ \ell \equiv \widehat{\ell} \pmod{te_0e_1'e_2'}}} \\ &\times \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \\ h_1e_1' \neq h_2e_2'}} \left\vert \sum_{\substack{k' \\ (k', e_1'e_2'\ell b) = 1}} g_0 \left(\frac{k'}{K/S}\right) \sum_{|j| \sim J} \textnormal{e}\left(j \omega \right)\, S\left( (h_1e_1' - h_2e_2')\, \overline{b \ell e_1' e_2'}, j; k's \right) \right\vert, \end{aligned} \] where \[ \omega = \omega(t, e_0, e_1', e_2', \widehat{\ell}, d, w) := \frac{d \overline{\widehat{\ell}}}{te_0e_1'e_2'} - w \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}. \] We now denote \[ m := h_1e_1' - h_2e_2' \ll \frac{HE}{E_0}, \qquad\qquad r := b \ell e_1' e_2' \asymp x^{O(\eta)} \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2}, \] split into dyadic ranges $m \sim M_=$, $r \sim R_=$, and change variables from $\ell$ to $r$ to obtain \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{\substack{M_= \ll HE/E_0 \\ R_= \asymp x^{O(\eta)} LE^2/E_0^2}}\, \sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\widehat{\ell} \in (\mathbf{Z}/te_0e_1'e_2'\mathbf{Z})^\times} \\ &\times \sum_{\substack{r \sim R_= \\ b e_1'e_2' \mid r \\ r/(be_1'e_2') \equiv \widehat{\ell} \\ \pmod{te_0e_1'e_2'}}} \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \\ (s, r) = 1 \\ s \mid te_0}} \sum_{m \sim M_=} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \\ h_1e_1' - h_2e_2' = m}} \left\vert \sum_{\substack{k' \\ (k', r) = 1}} g_0 \left(\frac{k'}{K/S}\right) \sum_{|j| \sim J} \textnormal{e}\left(j \omega \right)\, S\left(m \overline{r}, j; k's \right) \right\vert. \end{aligned} \] Crucially, note that once the variables $t, e_0, e_1', e_2', \widehat{\ell}$ are fixed, $\omega$ does not depend on $r, s, m, h_1, h_2, k'$ or $j$. Finally, we remove the absolute values by inserting $1$-bounded coefficients $\xi_{h_1,h_2}$ (also depending on $t, e_0, e_1', e_2', \widehat{\ell}, r, s, m$), and denote \[ a_{m,r,s} = a_{m,r,s}\left(t, e_0, e_1', e_2', \widehat{\ell}\right) := \mathbbm{1}_{b e_1'e_2' \mid r} \mathbbm{1}_{\substack{r/(be_1'e_2') \equiv \widehat{\ell} \\ \pmod{te_0e_1'e_2'}}} \mathbbm{1}_{s \mid te_0} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \\ h_1e_1' - h_2e_2' = m}} \xi_{h_1, h_2}, \] to get \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_{=} &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{\substack{M_= \ll HE/E_0 \\ R_= \asymp x^{O(\eta)} LE^2/E_0^2}}\, \sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\widehat{\ell} \in (\mathbf{Z}/te_0e_1'e_2'\mathbf{Z})^\times} |\mathcal{K}_{=}|, \end{aligned} \end{equation} with \[ \mathcal{K}_{=} := \sum_{\substack{r \sim R_= \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} \sum_{m \sim M_{=}} a_{m,r,s} \sum_{|j| \sim J} \textnormal{e}(j \omega) \sum_{\substack{k' \\ (k', r) = 1}} g_0 \left(\frac{k'}{K/S}\right)\, S\left(m\overline{r}, j; k's \right). \] At this point we apply our Deshouillers--Iwaniec-style bound from \cref{thm:di-type-bound}, finding that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_{=} \ll_\eta\ &x^{O(\eta)} \left(1 + \frac{K/S}{R_= \sqrt{S}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} ||a_{m,r,s}||_2 \, \sqrt{J R_= S} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2/S^2}{R_=} \left(M_{=} + R_=S\right)\left(J + R_=S\right) + M_{=}J \right)^{1/2}, \end{aligned} \] where by Cauchy--Schwarz, \[ \begin{aligned} &\sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0}\, \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\widehat{\ell} \in (\mathbf{Z}/te_0e_1'e_2'\mathbf{Z})^\times} ||a_{m,r,s}||_2 \\ &\ll \frac{TE^2}{E_0} \sqrt{\sum_{t \sim T} \sum_{e_0 \sim E_0} \sum_{\substack{e_1', e_2' \sim E/e_0 \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1}} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R_= \\ b e_1'e_2' \mid r}} \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \\ (s, r) = 1 \\ s \mid te_0}} \sum_{m \sim M_=} \left(\sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \sim H \\ h_1e_1' - h_2e_2' = m}} 1\right)^2 } \\ &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \frac{TE^2}{E_0} \sqrt{ TE_0 \frac{R_= E_0^2}{E^2} \sum_{m \sim M_{=}}\, \sum_{h_2 \sim H} \sum_{e_2' \ll E/E_0} \sum_{\substack{h_1, e_1' \\ (e_1', e_2') = 1 \\ h_1e_1' = m + h_2e_2'}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_1' \sim H \\ h_1'e_1' \equiv m \pmod{e_2'}}} \sum_{\substack{h_2' \sim H \\ h_2'e_2' = h_1'e_1' - m}} 1 } \\ &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \frac{TE^2}{E_0} \left(\frac{TE_0^3 R_=}{E^2} M_= H\frac{E}{E_0}\left(1 + \frac{HE_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \\ &= x^{O(\eta)} \left(T^3 E^3 R_= M_= H\left(1 + \frac{H E_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] Plugging these bounds into \cref{eq:b-eq-bound}, we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_{=} &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \sup_{\substack{M_= \ll HE/E_0 \\ R_= \asymp x^{O(\eta)} LE^2/E_0^2}}\, \left(1 + \frac{K/S}{R_= \sqrt{S}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(T^3 E^3 R_= M_= H\left(1 + \frac{H E_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \left(J R_= S\right)^{1/2} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2/S^2}{R_=} \left(M_{=} + R_=S\right)\left(J + R_=S\right) + M_{=}J \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] Using $M_= \ll HE/E_0$ and $R_= \asymp x^{O(\eta)} LE^2/E_0^2$, and recalling that $J \ll (KTE^2 x^\eta)/ (NE_0)$ (from \cref{lem:splitting-bfi}), we conclude that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \left(1 + \frac{KE_0^2}{LE^2S^{3/2}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(T^3 E^3 \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} \frac{HE}{E_0} H\left(1 + \frac{HE_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} S\right)^{1/2} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2 E_0^2}{L E^2 S^2} \left(\frac{HE}{E_0} + \frac{L E^2}{E_0^2} S\right)\left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} + \frac{L E^2}{E_0^2}S\right) + \frac{HKTE^3}{NE_0^2} \right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll x^{O(\eta)} \left(1 + \frac{KE_0^2}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(T^3 E^3 \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} \frac{HE}{E_0} H\left(1 + \frac{HE_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} \right)^{1/2} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2 E_0^2}{L E^2} \left(\frac{HE}{E_0 S} + \frac{L E^2}{E_0^2}\right)\left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} + \frac{L E^2}{E_0^2}S\right) + \frac{HKTE^3}{NE_0^2}S \right)^{1/2}, \end{aligned} \] where in the second line we grouped $S$-factors together (and lower-bounded $S \gg 1$ in the factor raised to $\theta_{\max}$). Since $1 \ll S \ll TE_0$ (from \cref{lem:splitting-bfi}), our bound becomes \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &\ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \left(1 + \frac{KE_0^2}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(T^3 E^3 \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} \frac{HE}{E_0} H\left(1 + \frac{HE_0}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} \frac{LE^2}{E_0^2} \right)^{1/2} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2 E_0^2}{L E^2} \left(\frac{HE}{E_0} + \frac{L E^2}{E_0^2}\right)\left(\frac{KTE^2}{NE_0} + \frac{L E^2 T}{E_0}\right) + \frac{HKT^2E^3}{NE_0} \right)^{1/2} \end{aligned} \] This expression is nonincreasing in $E_0$, even after extracting a factor of $E_0^{-1}$ (since $\theta_{\max} < 3/4$); thus lower-bounding $E_0 \gg 1$ we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &\ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)}}{E_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(T^3 E^6 L H^2 \left(1 + \frac{H}{E}\right)\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{KTLE^4}{N}\right)^{1/2} \\ &\times \left(\frac{K^2}{L E^2} \left(HE + L E^2\right)\left(\frac{KTE^2}{N} + L E^2 T\right) + \frac{HKT^2E^3}{N} \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] We can simplify this further using our assumption that $EHT \ll x^{O(\eta)} KNL$, which implies \[ x^{-O(\eta)} \frac{HKT^2E^3}{N} \ll K^2 L E^2 T = \frac{K^2}{LE^2} LE^2 LE^2T, \] allowing us to discard the term of $HKT^2E^3/N$ in the second line. Thus \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}_= &\ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)}}{E_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(1 + \frac{H}{E}\right)^{1/2} \left(T^3 E^6 L H^2 \frac{KTLE^4}{N} \right)^{1/2} \\ &\times K \left(\frac{H}{LE} + 1\right)^{1/2} \left(LE^2T\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{K}{NL} + 1 \right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll \frac{x^{O(\eta)}}{E_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(\frac{K^3T^5L^3E^{12}H^2}{N} \right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{H}{E} + \frac{H^2}{LE^2}\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL} \right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll \frac{x^{O(\eta)}}{E_0} \frac{KE^2}{N} \left(1 + \frac{K}{LE^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(KT^5L^3E^8H^2 N\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{H}{E} + \frac{H^2}{LE^2}\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL} \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] After slightly rearranging factors, this yields the desired bound.
nodes.statement_short: Remove the $\ell$-dependence of the phase, change variables to $r$, apply Theorem 3.9 and Cauchy–Schwarz, then optimize over $S$ and $E_0$.

nodes.name: Contribution of $\ell_1 \neq \ell_2$
nodes.statement: With the notation of \cref{lem:splitting-bfi}, assuming that $EHT \ll x^{O(\eta)} KNL$, one has \[ \mathcal{B}_{\neq} \ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)} K E^2}{NE_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{E^2 L^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(K T^4 E^8 H^2 L^6 N\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{H}{EL}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL^2}\right)^{1/2} \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound for $\mathcal B_{\neq}$ via the DI-type Kloosterman bound.
conclusions: \mathcal{B}_{\neq} \ll_\eta \frac{x^{O(\eta)} K E^2}{NE_0} \left(1 + \frac{K}{E^2 L^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \left(K T^4 E^8 H^2 L^6 N\right)^{1/2} \left(1 + \frac{H}{EL}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL^2}\right)^{1/2} \]
nodes.label: lem:split-bfi-neq

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.3 assuming Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement_short: Remove the $\ell_i$-dependence of the phase, extract $\ell_0=(\ell_1,\ell_2)$, apply Theorem 3.9 and Cauchy–Schwarz, then optimize over $L_0$, $S$, $E_0$.

nodes.name: BFI-style bound with general parameters
nodes.statement: For $\eta \in (0, 1)$, $K, N, T, E, H, L \ll x$, and any positive integers $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x$, assuming that $EHT \ll x^{O(\eta)} KNL$, one has \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{B}(K, N, T, E, H, L)^2 \ll_\eta\, &x^{O(\eta)} \Bigg( N^2 K^2 H^2 T^2 L^2 + K^2 E^2 H^2 T^4 L^2 + N^2 H^4 L^4 + N^2 H^4 T^2 L^2 \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{K^2}{E^4 L^4}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} K T^4 E^8 H^2 L^6 N \left(1 + \frac{H^2}{E^2L^2}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL^2}\right) \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{K^2}{E^4L^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} K T^5 E^8 H^2 L^3 N \left(1 + \frac{H}{E} + \frac{H^2}{E^2L}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL} \right) \Bigg). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: General bound for $\mathcal B^2$ in terms of $K,N,T,E,H,L$ and $\theta_{\max}$.
assumptions: For $\eta \in (0, 1)$, $K, N, T, E, H, L \ll x$
any positive integers $b \ll x^{O(\eta)}$ and $d \ll x$
conclusions: \mathcal{B}(K, N, T, E, H, L)^2 \ll_\eta\, &x^{O(\eta)} \Bigg( N^2 K^2 H^2 T^2 L^2 + K^2 E^2 H^2 T^4 L^2 + N^2 H^4 L^4 + N^2 H^4 T^2 L^2 \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{K^2}{E^4 L^4}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} K T^4 E^8 H^2 L^6 N \left(1 + \frac{H^2}{E^2L^2}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL^2}\right) \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{K^2}{E^4L^2}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} K T^5 E^8 H^2 L^3 N \left(1 + \frac{H}{E} + \frac{H^2}{E^2L}\right) \left(1 + \frac{K}{NL} \right) \Bigg). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.label: prop:bfi-expo-2

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9.4 assuming Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement: This follows by putting together \cref{lem:splitting-bfi,lem:split-bfi-neq,lem:split-bfi-eq} and squaring (the second line comes from \cref{lem:split-bfi-neq}, and the third line from \cref{lem:split-bfi-eq}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 9.1–9.3 and square.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.4 assuming Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement: Let $\theta := \theta_{\max}$; we will soon pick a value for $E$ such that \cref{eq:E-conditions} holds. We can assume without loss of generality that $K', N', T', E, H', L' \gg 1$, since otherwise the sum in \cref{prop:bfi-expo} is void. We now apply the bound in \cref{prop:bfi-expo-2} (which is increasing in all six parameters) for the parameters $K', N', T', E, H', L'$ from \cref{prop:bfi-expo}, noting that \[ \begin{aligned} EH'T' &\ll x^{O(\eta)} ERM^{-1} NL (ER)^{-1} \\ &= x^{O(\eta)} NL M^{-1} \ll x^{O(\eta)} NL \ll x^{O(\eta)} K' N' L'. \end{aligned} \] Plugging in the bounds $K' \ll NL x^{O(\eta)}$, $N' \asymp N x^{O(\eta)}$, $L' \asymp L x^{O(\eta)}$, $T' \ll NL(RE)^{-1} x^{O(\eta)}$, $H' \ll RNL x^{O(\eta)-1}$, we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathcal{B}(K', N', T', E, H', L')^2 \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} \\ &\quad \times \Bigg( N^2 (NL)^2 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2 \left(\frac{NL}{RE}\right)^2 L^2 + (NL)^2 E^2 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2 \left(\frac{NL}{RE}\right)^4 L^2 \\ &\quad + N^2 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^4 L^4 + N^2 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^4 \left(\frac{NL}{RE}\right)^2 L^2 \\ &\quad + \left(1 + \frac{(NL)^2}{E^4L^4}\right)^\theta NL \left(\frac{NL}{RE}\right)^4 E^8 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2 L^6 N \left(1 + \frac{\left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2}{E^2 L^2}\right) \\ &\quad + \left(1 + \frac{(NL)^2}{E^4L^2} \right)^\theta NL \left(\frac{NL}{RE}\right)^5 E^8 \left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2 L^3 N \left(1 + \frac{\left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)}{E} + \frac{\left(\frac{RNL}{x}\right)^2}{E^2 L}\right). \end{aligned} \] Simplifying terms and dividing both sides by $N^4 L^6$, we further get \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{\mathcal{B}(K', N', T', E, H', L')^2}{N^4 L^6} \ll_\eta x^{O(\eta)} &\Bigg( \frac{N^4 L^2}{x^2 E^2} + \frac{N^4 L^4}{R^2 x^2 E^2} + \frac{N^2 L^2 R^4}{x^4} + \frac{N^4 L^2 R^2}{x^4 E^2} \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4 L^2}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^4 L^7 E^4}{x^2 R^2} \left(1 + \frac{N^2 R^2}{x^2 E^2}\right) \\ &+ \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4} \right)^{\theta} \frac{N^5 L^5 E^3}{x^2 R^3} \left( 1 + \frac{NLR}{xE} + \frac{N^2 L R^2}{x^2 E^2} \right) \Bigg), \end{aligned} \] and we wish to show that the right-hand side is $\ll x^{O(\eta) - \varepsilon}$. To handle the first term of $N^4 L^2 x^{-2} E^{-2}$, we require that $N^2 L \ll x^{1-\varepsilon} E$; thus we pick \begin{equation} E := \max\left( x^{4\varepsilon}, \frac{N^2 L}{x^{1-\varepsilon}} \right). \end{equation} For \cref{eq:E-conditions} to hold, we also need to have $E \ll x^{-\varepsilon} NL R^{-1}$, so we impose the restrictions \[ R \ll x^{-5\varepsilon} NL \qquad\quad \text{and} \qquad\quad N \ll \frac{x^{1-2\varepsilon}}{R} \] (which are part of \cref{eq:conditions}). The fact that $NR \ll x$ simplifies our expression a bit; combined with the fact that $E \ll x^{-\varepsilon} N L R^{-1} \ll NL R x^{-1}$ (due to $x^{1-\varepsilon} \ll R^2$ from \cref{eq:conditions}), this shows that \[ \frac{N^2 R^2}{x^2 E^2} \ll 1 \qquad\quad \text{and} \qquad\quad \max\left(\frac{N^2 L R^2}{x^2 E^2}, 1\right) \ll \frac{N L R}{x E}. \] Moreover, since $x^{(1-\varepsilon)/2} \ll R$ by \cref{eq:conditions}, we have $NR \ll x^{1-2\varepsilon} \ll R^2$, so $N \ll R$, which implies \[ \frac{N^4 L^2 R^2}{x^4 E^2} \ll \frac{N^2 L^2 R^4}{x^4}. \] Overall, it remains to bound the expression \begin{equation} \frac{N^4 L^4}{R^2 E^2 x^2} + \frac{N^2 L^2 R^4}{x^4} + \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4 L^2}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^4 L^7 E^4}{x^2 R^2} + \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^6 L^6 E^2}{x^3 R^2} \end{equation} by $O(x^{-\varepsilon})$. Using $x^{(1-\varepsilon)/2} \ll R \ll NL \ll x^{2/3 - 6\varepsilon}$ (from \cref{eq:conditions}) and $E \ge x^{4\varepsilon}$, the first term is admissible since \[ \frac{N^2 L^2}{REx} \ll \frac{x^{4/3}}{x^{3\varepsilon} x^{3/2}} = x^{-1/6 - 3\varepsilon}. \] The (square root of the) second term is similarly bounded: \[ \frac{NL R^2}{x^2} \ll x^{(2/3) + (4/3) - 2 - 6\varepsilon} = x^{- 6\varepsilon}. \] For the third term in \cref{eq:final-to-bound}, we use our choice of $E$ from \cref{eq:E-choice} to obtain \[ \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4 L^2}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^4 L^7 E^4}{x^2 R^2} \ll \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{L^2}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^4 L^7}{x^{2-16\varepsilon} R^2} + \left(1 + \frac{x^4}{N^6 L^6}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^{12} L^{11}}{x^{6-4\varepsilon} R^2}. \] Since $NL \ll x^{2/3}$ by \cref{eq:conditions}, we can ignore the $1$-term in the last parenthesis. For the terms above to be admissible, we require the restrictions \[ N^4 L^7 \max(1, N/L)^{2\theta} \ll x^{2-16\varepsilon}R^2, \qquad\quad N^{12-6\theta} L^{11-6\theta} \ll x^{6-4(\theta+\varepsilon)} R^2 \] (which are part of \cref{eq:conditions}). Finally, using that $1 \ll E \ll x^{-\varepsilon} NLR^{-1}$ (from \cref{eq:E-conditions}), we crudely bound the fourth and last term in \cref{eq:final-to-bound} by \[ \left(1 + \frac{N^2}{E^4}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^6 L^6 E^2}{x^3 R^2} \ll N^{2\theta} \frac{N^6 L^6 (x^{-\varepsilon}NLR^{-1})^2}{x^3 R^2} \ll x^{-2\varepsilon} \frac{N^9 L^8}{x^3 R^4}, \] which is at most $O(x^{-\varepsilon})$ by the last condition in the first line of \cref{eq:conditions}. This completes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Plug the parameter sizes into Proposition 9.4, choose $E$, and check each term against the conditions (4.2).

nodes.name: Maass cusp form basis and Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement: In particular, we consider an orthonormal basis of Maass cusp forms $(u_{j,q})_{j \ge 1}$ such that $u_{j,q}$ has eigenvalue $\lambda_{j,q}$ (which increases to $\infty$ as $j \to \infty$), and Fourier coefficients $\rho_{j,\mathfrak{a}}(n)$ when expanding around the cusp $\mathfrak{a}$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$, via an implicit scaling matrix $\sigma_{\mathfrak{a}} \in \textnormal{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$.

nodes.name: Cusp width $\mu(\mathfrak{a})$
nodes.statement: We denote \[ \mu(\mathfrak{a}) := \frac{\left(w, \frac{q}{w}\right)}{q}, \] whenever $\mathfrak{a}$ is equivalent to $u/w$, for some relatively prime $u, w \in \mathbf{Z}_+$ such that $w \mid q$; in particular, one has $\mu(\infty) = q^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Spectral parameters $\theta_{j,q}$, $\kappa_{j,q}$
nodes.statement: We also write \[ \theta_{j,q} := 2i \kappa_{j,q}, \qquad\qquad \kappa_{j,q}^2 = \lambda_{j,q} - \frac{1}{4} \qquad \iff \qquad \theta_{j,q}^2 = 1 - 4\lambda_{j,q}, \] where $\kappa_{j,q}$ is chosen such that either $\kappa_{j,q} \ge 0$ (when $\lambda_{j,q} \ge 1/4$), or $i\kappa_{j,q} > 0$ (when $\lambda_{j,q}$ is exceptional).

nodes.name: Exceptional eigenvalues lie in $[3/16, 1/4)$
nodes.statement: Also, recall that all exceptional eigenvalues lie in the interval $[3/16, 1/4)$ by \cite[Theorem 4]{deshouillers1982kloosterman} (in fact, the best currently known lower bound is $975/4096$, due to Kim--Sarnak \cite[Appendix 2]{kim2003functoriality}; this is equivalent to \cref{thm:kim-sarnak}).
conclusions: all exceptional eigenvalues lie in the interval $[3/16, 1/4)$

nodes.name: Large sieve inequalities from Deshouillers–Iwaniec
nodes.statement: Given $\varepsilon > 0$, $q \in \mathbf{Z}_+$, $N \gg 1$, a complex sequence $(a_n)_{n \sim N}$, a cusp $\mathfrak{a}$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$, and an associated scaling matrix $\sigma_{\mathfrak{a}}$, one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{j \ge 1 \\ \lambda_{j,q} < 1/4}} X^{\theta_{j,q}} \left\vert \sum_{n \sim N} a_n\, \rho_{j,\mathfrak{a}}(n) \right\vert^2 \ll_\varepsilon (QN)^\varepsilon \left(1 + \mu(\mathfrak{a}) N\right) ||a_n||_2^2, \end{equation} for any $0 < X \ll \max(1, \mu(\mathfrak{a})^{-1}N^{-1})$. Moreover, if $(\mathfrak{a}, \sigma_{\mathfrak{a}}) = (\infty, \textnormal{Id})$, then given $Q \gg 1$ and $\alpha \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}$, one has \begin{equation} \frac{1}{Q} \sum_{q \sim Q} \sum_{\substack{j \ge 1 \\ \lambda_{j,q} < 1/4}} X^{\theta_{j,q}} \left\vert \sum_{n \sim N} \textnormal{e}(n\omega)\, \rho_{j,\infty}(n) \right\vert^2 \ll_\varepsilon (QN)^\varepsilon \left(1 + Q^{-1}N\right) N, \end{equation} in the larger range $0 < X \ll \max\left(N, Q^2 N^{-1}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: Large sieve inequalities for Fourier coefficients of exceptional Maass forms, weighted by $X^{\theta_{j,q}}$.
assumptions: Given $\varepsilon > 0$, $q \in \mathbf{Z}_+$, $N \gg 1$, a complex sequence $(a_n)_{n \sim N}$, a cusp $\mathfrak{a}$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$, and an associated scaling matrix $\sigma_{\mathfrak{a}}$
in the larger range $0 < X \ll \max\left(N, Q^2 N^{-1}\right)$.
in the larger range $0 < X \ll \max\left(N, Q^2 N^{-1}\right)$.

nodes.label: lem:di-large-sieve

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10.1
nodes.statement: The bounds in \cref{eq:like-di-thm-5,eq:like-di-thm-7} follow immediately from \cite[Theorems 5 and 7]{deshouillers1982kloosterman} respectively. We note that changing the choice of the scaling matrix $\sigma_{\mathfrak{a}}$ results in multiplying the Fourier coefficients $\rho_{j,\mathfrak{a}}(n)$ by an exponential phase $\textnormal{e}(n\omega)$; thus in \cref{eq:like-di-thm-7}, using an arbitrary value of $\omega$ is equivalent to using an arbitrary (but consistent) choice of the scaling matrix $\sigma_\infty$. We also remark that the proof of \cite[Theorem 7]{deshouillers1982kloosterman} from \cite[\S 8.3]{deshouillers1982kloosterman} only considers the case $\omega = 0$ (and $\sigma_\infty = \textnormal{Id}$), but the same proof extends to any $\omega \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}$ (or equivalently, to any valid scaling matrix $\sigma_\infty$); this was already noted, for instance, in \cite[Lemma 5]{bombieri1987primes2}. Ultimately, this is because the proof of \cite[Theorem 14]{deshouillers1982kloosterman} also extends to sums with additional weights of $\textnormal{e}(m\omega_1)\, \textnormal{e}(n\omega_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Deshouillers–Iwaniec Theorems 5 and 7, noting the extension to arbitrary phase $\omega$.

nodes.name: Equivalence with DI's large sieve formulations
nodes.statement: The large sieve inequalities in \cite{deshouillers1982kloosterman} are stated for general values of $X$ in the left-hand sides (resulting in right-hand sides that depend on $X$), and are equivalent to those given in \cref{lem:di-large-sieve}. Indeed, to recover large sieve inequalities with an arbitrary $X > 0$ in the left-hand sides, it suffices to multiply the right-hand sides by $(1 + (X/X_0)^{\theta_q})$, where $X_0$ is the best allowable value in \cref{lem:di-large-sieve}. We find the versions stated above easier to apply optimally in the $\theta$-aspect, and also easier to compare, by contrasting the maximal permitted values of $X$ (recalling that $\mu(\infty) = q^{-1}$).

nodes.name: Deshouillers–Iwaniec-type multilinear Kloosterman bound
nodes.statement: Let $C, M, N, R, S \gg 1$, $(b_{n,r,s})$ be a complex sequence, and $\omega \in \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z}$.
